title: Rumble's Shiny Crumb Trail
markdown:
Once, in the tall snowy Frostcap Range, where wind whistled tunes through the rocky tops, lived a young ogre named Rumble. He had large feet and a bumpy nose that wiggled when he thought, and a heart as warm as a marshmallow just off the fire. He was not the sort of ogre old stories like to growl about.

That evening the moon hung like a round milky cheese. The bluebell wood below his cave lay in soft light, quiet and twinkly. Rumble’s toes wiggled. “A little walk,” he rumbled, thunder far off and friendly. “Just a quiet peek.”

Corvus sat on a mossy rock outside, a crow with feathers like midnight and eyes like bright black beads. He crackled a cheerful caw. Moonlight walks suited him too.

Rumble asked if he was ready. Corvus puffed, shimmered, and answered in the way of crows, which Rumble heard as always.

So Rumble, with Corvus perched comfortably on his broad sturdy shoulder, hopped down from the warm cave. They landed softly on the grassy hillside and walked toward the bluebell wood. The bluebells were periwinkle, a summer sky after rain, carpeting the forest floor, and under the moon they twinkled like tiny fallen stars. It was peaceful. Rumble hummed a soft oafish tune, a happy rumbling melody that blended with whispering leaves.

Corvus suddenly tilted his head. His bright eyes had seen something. He pointed his beak toward the winding path.

Crumbs. Little tiny sprinkled crumbs on the mossy trail, like a fairy’s dropped treasure. They were not ordinary. They shimmered with a soft gentle golden light, as if they had captured bits of the moonbeams themselves.

“Ooh, shiny,” Rumble whispered, bumpy nose wiggling with curiosity. Corvus hopped off the shoulder, pecked a particularly bright crumb, found it wonderfully sweet and a little nutty, and chirped, hopping from one glowing crumb to another.

Rumble could not resist. He followed the glowing trail, large feet making soft thuds on yielding ground, deeper into the woods. Trees grew closer, branches a leafy roof, shadows dancing more playfully. His feet were surprisingly quiet on the soft damp earth, Corvus darting ahead.

He paused, brow furrowed just a little. This was a bit further than he usually went from his cave. The bluebells seemed to whisper secrets to each other, delicate petals swaying.

Corvus was still keen. He flitted ahead, dark wings catching moonlight. More shiny. Come on, Rumble.

The clearing they reached should not have been sun-dappled at night, yet it was. In the middle stood a cottage no bigger than a very large mushroom. Cinnamon smoke curled from a tiny chimney. At a wooden table a small goblin stirred a clay bowl: twinkling eyes, pointed nose, flour-dusted apron, the look of someone busily kind.

He had never seen an ogre up close, and certainly not a young friendly one. His eyes widened like saucers.

“Well, hello. Who might you be, wandering so deep?”

Rumble shuffled. “I’m Rumble. This is Corvus. We followed some glowing crumbs.”

The goblin chuckled like silver bells. “My glow-crumb trail for berry buns. A secret way to guide friends to my door.” He gestured at the bowl. “I’m Pipkin, the baker. Fresh batch. Still warm. Would you like to try one? Sweetest juiciest berries you can imagine.”

Rumble’s worry melted. His tummy gurgled. Corvus landed on the table edge and nodded at the bowl.

Pipkin bustled with surprising speed for such a small creature. He soon presented Rumble with a bun as big as his fist, still steaming gently. It smelled heavenly: warm sunshine, ripe summer berries, a hint of something delightfully sweet. Rumble took a big bite, and his eyes lit with pure joy. It was the most delicious wonderful thing he had ever tasted. Corvus pecked a tiny berry that had fallen onto the table, chirping with absolute delight.

A tiny puff of warm air came from behind a flour sack. A head poked out: scales the colour of a new emerald leaf, glowing golden eyes, a dragon hatchling no bigger than a loaf, wings folded. Pipkin smiled. “This is Flicker. My little helper. He loves berry buns too. A bit shy.”

Flicker puffed cinnamon-scented air. Rumble forgot shyness, broke off a piece, and offered it. Flicker nibbled. His tail wiggled in the dust.

Pipkin saw Rumble’s eyelids droop. “Don’t you worry about getting home. The glow-crumb trail can lead you back to your cave.” He sprinkled extra-bright crumbs. Rumble walked with Corvus on his shoulder and Flicker fluttering nearby, a happy sigh carrying him along the golden line until the cave was familiar again, mossy rock and all.

And so Rumble learned that wandering a little farther than you meant to is not the same as being lost, not when the path is made of kindness. New friends may keep a cottage like a mushroom and a hatchling behind a flour sack. Treats may sing in your tummy. The same crumbs that tempted you on can light you home, if you follow them with a soft heart and leave the shiny things where a baker meant them to be.
